families.name: SR: Systemic-shock liquidity-provision reversal (beta- and segment-adjusted, news-filtered, long)
families.source_lens: Empirical asset pricing (designer 1, family A: rule, benchmark, signature). Merged with two other proposals: the options practitioner's family A (cash-secured-put expression, stress threshold) and the risk manager's R3 (same events and mechanism; its equal-risk sizing is used live). Holm family, slot 1 of 2.
families.mechanism:
On a systemic day (the fear model's shock-type label: at least 10% of eligible names dipped 2 own-sigma or more), much of the selling is not driven by information. It comes from de-grossing of crowded AI longs, thematic and leveraged-ETF flows, and volatility-target and margin sales.

Liquidity providers absorb this selling. They earn a premium that rises with market stress, because their capital and risk capacity shrink (Campbell, Grossman & Wang 1993 QJE; Brunnermeier & Pedersen 2009 RFS; Hameed, Kang & Viswanathan 2010 JF; Nagel 2012 RFS; Hendershott & Menkveld 2014 JFE). New capital arrives slowly, so the reversal plays out over days (Mitchell, Pedersen & Pulvino 2007 AER; Duffie 2010 JF). ETF arbitrage passes non-fundamental flow shocks on to the constituents (Ben-David, Franzoni & Moussawi 2018 JF; Coval & Stafford 2007 JFE).

Industry and segment moves carry information and momentum, while the residual within an industry reverses (Moskowitz & Grinblatt 1999 JF; Da, Liu & Schaumburg 2014 Management Science; Hameed & Mian 2015 JFQA). The rule therefore buys the residual left after removing beta and the segment move. Drops that came with the stock's own overnight news are excluded, because news-driven moves drift rather than reverse (Chan 2003 JFE; Savor 2012 JFE).

What the fear model supplies: the shock-type label, the own-sigma yardstick (sigma, x) and the stress dose (M_pct).

How this differs from the tests that already failed:
- It does not time the market (M predicting basket returns: Hodrick t 0.70).
- It is not the pooled raw-return study of Z >= 2.5, whose sign flipped.
- It is a cross-sectional, beta-adjusted, segment-relative rule, applied on systemic days only.
families.entry_rule:
The signal is computed at the close of t from signals.RuleFeatures: point-in-time refits in backtests, frozen v3 live, and prices up to t.

(1) Day: systemic_t, meaning share_hit2_t >= 0.10, where share_hit2_t is the share of fear-model-eligible names with x >= 2 at t. The day must also not be an NYSE early close (half_day_t): 2024-07-03, 2024-11-29, 2024-12-24, 2025-07-03, 2025-11-28, 2025-12-24, 2026-07-02, 2026-11-27.

(2) Name i must be:
- eligible_i,t;
- price_ok: raw close_t >= $5;
- liquid20: median of close x volume over t-20..t-1 >= $20M.

(3) Participation: x_i,t >= 2.

(4) Residual displacement: v_i,t <= -1.5.
- rB_t = equal-weight mean of eligible names' log return r at t.
- beta_i,t = (2/3) x OLS slope of r_i on rB over t-126..t-1 (at least 100 observations) + 1/3.
- u_i,t = (r_i,t - beta_i,t x rB_t) / sigma_i,t.
- v_i,t = u_i,t minus the median u of eligible names in i's segment at t. If the segment has fewer than 3 eligible names, use the median over all eligible names.

(5) News filter: g_seg_i,t > -2.
- gamma_i,t = ln(adj_open_t / adj_close_t-1) / sigma_i,t.
- g_seg_i,t = gamma_i,t minus the segment median gamma (same fallback).

(6) Not already held by this variant (signals.suppress_reentry with this variant's H). A name cannot be selected again until t+H, when the old position is sold at the same open the new one would be bought. Re-qualifying while held neither adds to the position nor resets its clock.

(7) Cap: at most 10 new names per signal day, the most negative v first (cap=10, priority=v).

Variant-specific changes are listed under variants.
families.execution:
Test, used by every gate:
- Buy at the official open of t+1 (engine delay=1) and sell at the open of t+1+H.
- Costs: 10 bps per side (25 bps stress test).
- The name also needs engine tradability: a close at t, an open at t+1, and a 20-session median dollar volume of at least $5M.

Gate series: the calendar-time portfolio ct_excess_net (Fama 1998).
- Each session, equal weight across all open SR positions.
- Each position's daily return is measured against beta_i,t x the daily return of the equal-weight basket of all tradable names bought at the same open.
- Costs are charged on entry and exit days.
- The series is 0 on sessions with no open position.

Also reported: the 1/H-cohort series excess_net. Each of the last H cohorts holds 1/H of the sleeve, with equal weight inside the cohort; a day without a signal leaves its 1/H in cash.

Delay check: enter at the open of t+2 and exit H sessions later.

Live:
- Shares through market-on-open orders at t+1, or the option expression below.
- Sizes come from the sizing framework (risk-budgeted, not equal weight).
- The simulated live sleeve is reported but is never a selection input.
families.exit_rule:
Shares: time exit only, selling at the official open of t+1+H with a market-on-open order. No stop-loss and no profit target.

CSP version: held to expiry with no early buy-back. Assigned shares are sold at the next open. After an early assignment, the shares are held to the planned expiry and sold at the next open.

Long-call version: sold at the expiry-day close if in the money; never exercised.
variants: SR1 (primary): rule as stated, H = 5 sessions.
SR2: as SR1 with H = 10 sessions (slow-moving capital).
SR3: as SR1, but only on signal days with M_pct_t >= 1.0 (the fear model's market percentile score at the close of t; Nagel's stress dose). H = 5.

SR4: as SR1 but with a beta-only residual. Condition (4) uses u_i,t <= -1.5 instead of v. Condition (5) uses g_all_i,t > -2 (gamma minus the median gamma of all eligible names) instead of g_seg. The cap ranks by u. H = 5. Tests whether segment-wide, thematic-ETF displacement also reverses.
families.benchmark:
Per event: e = R_i - beta_i,t x R_B - round-trip cost.
- R_i and R_B are the open(t+1) to open(t+1+H) total returns of the name and of the equal-weight basket of all tradable names, bought and sold at the same opens.
- beta_i,t is the shrunk trailing beta from the signal (Variant beta_benchmark=True).

Gate statistic: mean daily ct_excess_net over 2024-01-02..2025-12-31, using only cohorts that exit by 2025-12-31. Its s.e. comes from the stationary-bootstrap long-run variance (mean block 20). Side long; Holm family.

Reported alongside:
- the plain-basket excess (beta = 1);
- the same-stock-adjusted excess e - base_i(H), where base_i(H) = backtest.same_stock_baseline(rf, prices, H, dev) is stock i's mean H-session beta-adjusted excess over every dev session. This strips out the hindsight drift of the AI winners.
families.predicted_signature:
Predicted:
- Mean net excess of +0.5% to +1.5% per 5-session event: 0.2-0.6 own-sigma, or 10-30% of the median 2.0-sigma residual displacement.
- It accrues mostly in sessions 1-5, and at least half is still present at session 20 (a permanent reversal of price pressure).

REQUIRED for gate (c), on the chosen variant's dev events:
- (S1) Not realized beta: in an OLS of event excess e on [1, R_B] (trades.basket_ret), with CR1 errors clustered by signal date (gates.ols_cluster), the intercept a > 0.
- (S2) Shock-type contrast: the chosen variant's mean e exceeds that of the identical rule with condition (1) replaced by 'not systemic_t'. Everything else stays unchanged: any M_pct condition, H, cap and priority. For SR1 the contrast has 473 dev events on 242 days. Nagel predicts the liquidity premium is larger in stress.
- (S3) Hindsight guard: the mean over events of (e - base_i(H)) > 0.

REPORTED, not gating:
- Slope of e on M_pct_t is > 0 (CR1 by day), and SR3 >= SR1 per event.
- Front-loading: sessions 1-3 carry more than half of the H=5 excess.
- Permanence: the mean excess measured to session 20 is at least half the H-session excess.
- The news-excluded systemic set (x >= 2, v <= -1.5, g_seg <= -2; 131 dev events) earns less, because it drifts.
- The most-displaced v tercile (v <= -2.27 on dev SR1 events) beats the least displaced.
- The effect is larger in the less liquid half.
- At least half survives the one-day delay.
- The sign survives leaving out any one of the 25 dev clusters.
- If SR4 beats SR1, the gain concentrates in compute, semicap and foundry/memory, the segments with the heaviest ETF flows.
families.power_note:
Counts use signal-side data only and no outcomes. Inputs are point-in-time, counted after no-re-entry and the cap, for dev signals whose cohorts exit by 2025-12-31. Scripts: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fear-signal/746ee66c-3d9a-5a30-89ca-deab40db82a0/scratchpad/judge_counts.py through judge_counts4.py.

Dev period:
- SR1: 490 events on 122 signal days, in 25 clusters (gap > 5 sessions) or 12 (gap > 10). 64 distinct weeks, 123 tickers (the top 5 hold 10%). Every dev quarter has 28-99 events.
- SR1 signal days by M_pct: 46 below 1, 22 in 1-1.5, 23 in 1.5-2, 12 in 2-2.5, 19 at 2.5 or above.
- SR1 medians: sigma 2.29%/day, beta 0.92, v -2.01.
- SR2: 459 events on 118 days.
- SR3: 328 events on 77 days (16 clusters).
- SR4: 659 events on 123 days.

2026 holdout (partly seen: the event study used different rules):
- SR1: 294 events on 70 days (10 clusters).
- SR3: 146 events on 37 days.
- SR4: 442 events on 73 days.

Power:
- Per-event 5-session residual s.d. is about 6-7%, with roughly 60-80 effectively independent cohorts.
- t is about 1.6-2.1 at +1.0% net per event, about 2.4-3 at +1.5%, and about 1-1.3 at +0.6%.
- Clearing the calibrated SPA_c (4 correlated variants) at the Holm threshold of 0.05 needs about +1.0-1.3% per event (0.45-0.55 own-sigma).
- Prior chance of adoption: about 25-30%. This is the most powerful family on offer: 25 dev clusters and 490 stock-events, against 4 episodes for the market-level M >= 2 test.

Thresholds and bias:
- SR3 uses M_pct >= 1.0 rather than 1.5. Point-in-time M_pct is at least 1.0 on 30% of dev sessions and 32% of 2026 sessions, which is stable. It is at least 1.5 on 18% of dev sessions but only 9% of 2026 sessions, which is not.
- The hindsight universe inflates buy-the-dip results. S3 and the same-stock check guard against this; only the prospective paper test is clean.
families.options_expression:
Default is shares. The instrument is chosen per ticket at the close of t from the live Robinhood chain and plays no part in selection.

(a) Candidate contract: the put with delta nearest -0.35 (accept -0.25 to -0.45), at the first listed expiry with h >= H and h <= H+5 sessions from entry (t+1 counts as session 1).

Filters (if any fails, use shares):
- quoted spread <= 10% of mid;
- open interest >= 250;
- mid >= $0.30;
- no earnings date between t+1 and expiry (Robinhood earnings calendar);
- 100 x strike <= the ticket's notional;
- put IV minus the IV of the same-strike, same-expiry call <= 5 vol points. Expensive puts signal borrow stress or informed selling (Ofek, Richardson & Whitelaw 2004; Cremers & Weinbaum 2010).

(b) Richness: rho = IV_put x sqrt(D/365) / sigma_tilde_i(h).
- D = calendar days from t+1 to expiry.
- sigma_tilde_i(h) = the framework's h-session forward s.d.: the fear model's regime forecast, shrunk and level-calibrated, or EWMA if that forecast failed validation.

(c) Choice:
- rho >= 1.25: sell a cash-secured put, contracts = floor(notional / (100 x strike)). If the same-strike call IV >= put IV + 2 vol points, do the equivalent buy-write instead: buy 100 x contracts shares at the open and sell that call.
- rho <= 0.90: buy the call nearest +0.60 delta under the same expiry rule. Dollar delta about equal to the notional; premium <= min(30% of notional, 1% of NAV).
- Otherwise: shares.

(d) Orders:
- Options go in as limits at mid, conceding at most 1/4 of the quoted spread, between 09:45 and 10:30 ET on t+1.
- If unfilled at 10:30, buy shares at market (logged as a deviation).
- No option orders on half-days.
- No covered calls against SR shares beyond the CSP's buy-write twin, because they would sell the predicted rebound.

Why a CSP: on systemic days, short-dated single-stock puts are rich.
- The IV term structure inverts (Vasquez 2017).
- Put-buying pressure meets constrained dealers (Bollen & Whaley 2004; Garleanu, Pedersen & Poteshman 2009).
- Variance premia peak after volatility spikes (Bollerslev, Tauchen & Zhou 2009).
- IV far above forecast volatility predicts low option returns (Goyal & Saretto 2009).
- The panic regime lasts about 2 sessions.
So a CSP collects the premium while staying long the predicted rebound. Shares win in a sharp V-shaped rebound, because the CSP caps the upside at the premium.

Enablement check, after adoption:
- Draw up to 12 expired contracts on SR dev events, seeded and stratified by episode.
- Back out the entry-day IV with options.implied_vol, using the mean of open and close for both the option and the underlying.
- The CSP branch is enabled only if the median actual rho >= 1.25 and at least 8 of the 12 have actual rho >= 1.0. Otherwise trade shares only.
- A price-only replay at IV = lambda x model volatility (lambda 0.80-2.00, step 0.05) reports the CSP's break-even lambda as a diagnostic. It sets no parameter.

families.name: ND: Idiosyncratic news-shock drift (bearish information; typed exits and long puts)
families.source_lens: Options practitioner (designer 3, family B: rule and put expression), merged with the risk manager's R2 (shock-typed exits). R2's exclusion window becomes ND's H. R2's test (sell the name and spread the proceeds over the basket) equals the short-information cohort test up to 1/N scaling. Holm family, slot 2 of 2. The slot is free: with two Holm families, both thresholds are 0.05.
families.entry_rule:
The signal is computed at the close of t from RuleFeatures; definitions are as in SR.
(1) NOT systemic_t (share_hit2_t < 0.10), and NOT half_day_t.
(2) eligible_i,t, price_ok (raw close >= $5) and liquid20 (median dollar volume over t-20..t-1 >= $20M).
(3) x_i,t >= 3: the low was at least 3 own-sigma below the previous close.
(4) v_i,t <= -2: the stock closed at least 2 own-sigma below its segment's median beta residual. The loss is stock-specific and had not recovered by the close.
(5) g_seg_i,t <= -2: a stock-specific overnight gap-down of at least 2 own-sigma relative to its segment, meaning the news came out outside market hours.
(6) Not already inside this variant's window (signals.suppress_reentry with this variant's H).
(7) Cap: at most 5 new names per day, the most negative v first (cap=5, priority=v).
families.execution:
Not traded as shares, because the account cannot short.

Information test, used by every gate (Variant side='short_info', beta_benchmark=True):
- Each event's short-side excess = beta_i,t x R_B - R_i - round-trip cost, over open(t+1) to open(t+1+H).
- Costs: 10 bps per side (25 bps stress test).
- Gate series ct_excess_net: each session, equal weight across all open ND events of their daily short-side excess; 0 when none is open.
- The 1/H-cohort series is reported.
- Delay check: the window starts at the open of t+2.

Live, only if ND is adopted:
- (i) Typed exit (tier >= 1): any core holding of the name is sold with a market-on-open order at t+1 and not re-bought before the open of t+1+H. SR positions keep their own time exits, so live SR still matches its test.
- (ii) Long put (tier >= 2; paper-logged otherwise): bought 09:45-10:30 ET on t+1 per the options expression. No ND put on a name SR currently holds.
families.exit_rule:
Information test: closes at the open of t+1+H (time exit, no stops).

Typed exit: the name may be bought again from the open of t+1+H.

Put: sold on session t+1+H between 09:45 and 10:30 ET, as a limit at mid conceding at most 1/4 of the spread, or at the close of the expiry day if that comes first. Never exercised, because exercising a put would create a short.
variants: ND1 (primary): rule as stated, H = 20 sessions.
ND2: as ND1 with H = 40 sessions (toward the 60-day PEAD window).
ND3: as ND1 with H = 10 sessions (modern drift, if any, comes early).
families.benchmark:
Beta x the equal-weight basket, on the short-information side. Per event: e = beta_i,t x R_B - R_i - round-trip cost, with the same windows, basket and beta as SR.

Gate: mean ct_excess_net over dev, using only cohorts that exit by 2025-12-31, with a stationary-bootstrap s.e. (block 20). Holm family.

Reported: the plain-basket version and the same-stock-adjusted version (base_i(H) with its sign flipped). Neither is required, because the hindsight bias already runs against a bearish signal.
families.predicted_signature:
Predicted: short-side excess of +1% to +3% per 20-session event, accruing gradually (a drift, not a one-day continuation).

REQUIRED for gate (c), on the chosen variant's dev events:
- (N1) Not beta: in an OLS of e on [1, R_B], with CR1 errors clustered by signal date, the intercept a > 0.
- (N2) Gradual: the mean cumulative short-side excess from the entry open to the close of session 2 is at most 1/3 of the mean H-session excess, which must itself be > 0.
- (N3) Information split: the chosen variant's mean e exceeds that of the no-news contrast rule. The contrast is identical except that condition (5) becomes g_seg_i,t > -1 (an intraday, no-gap stock-specific drop), with the same H, cap 5, priority v and side short_info; it has 96 dev events at H = 20. News drifts and no-news does not (Chan 2003; Savor 2012).

REPORTED:
- Typed contrast: the identical rule on systemic days (105 dev events) earns less short-side excess, if those hits are partly flow.
- The second half of the window carries at least 40% of the excess.
- The effect is larger in less liquid names: the CR1 slope of e on log 20-session median dollar volume is negative.
- Dose: v <= -5.15 (the most negative dev tercile) against the rest, and x >= 4 against 3 <= x < 4.
- The sign of the same-stock-adjusted excess.
families.power_note:
Counts use signal-side data only. Inputs are point-in-time, counted after no-re-entry and the cap, for dev cohorts that exit by 2025-12-31.

Dev period:
- ND1 (H20): 145 events on 104 days, 67 distinct weeks, 84 tickers (the top 5 hold 14%), 10-24 per dev quarter.
- ND1 medians: x 5.7, g_seg -4.0, sigma 2.24%/day. On 80 of the 104 signal days, M_pct was below 1.
- ND2 (H40): 135 events. ND3 (H10): 154 events.

2026 holdout: ND1 54, ND2 50, ND3 58 events.

Power:
- Events are firm-specific and spread out in time, so the effective N is close to the count.
- The 20-session residual s.d. is about 11-13% per event, giving a s.e. of about 1.0%. Reaching t of about 2 needs about +2.0-2.2% short-side excess per event.
- The 2026 read alone (s.e. about 1.7%) can confirm only effects of about 1.7% or more.
- Prior chance of adoption: about 10%.

Why it is kept: its Holm slot is free (m = 2), and because the bias runs against it, a pass would be credible.
families.options_expression:
Live only; never used in selection.

(a) Typed exit (adopted ND, tier >= 1): sell held shares at the t+1 open. This is the cheapest bearish expression.

A holder who must keep the shares (for tax reasons, or as a core position) may instead write a 30-45 DTE covered call, delta nearest +0.30. Only if rho >= 1.25, which is rare because post-earnings IV is usually crushed.

(b) Standalone long put, tier >= 2 only (paper otherwise):
- The put with delta nearest -0.35 (accept -0.25 to -0.45), at the first listed expiry with h >= H and h <= H+10 sessions from entry.
- Filters: spread <= 10% of mid; OI >= 250; mid >= $0.30.
- Buy only if rho = IV_put x sqrt(D/365) / sigma_tilde_i(h) <= 0.90, i.e. never pay more than the fear model's own (shrunk, calibrated) forward volatility.
- Premium <= 0.5% of NAV per name, and <= 2% of NAV across all open ND puts.
- Limit at mid, conceding at most 1/4 of the spread, 09:45-10:30 ET on t+1. If unfilled, skip it: the premium decays, so do not chase.

The model over-forecasts volatility after idiosyncratic hits (F5), which biases rho DOWN for these names. The halfway shrinkage of the regime multiplier and the dev level calibration in sigma_tilde partly correct this, and the 0.90 threshold is deliberately strict.

Why puts rarely beat doing nothing: a 5-week 35-delta put at 50% IV costs about 4% of spot, so the stock must fall about 9% in absolute terms to break even at expiry. That compares with a plausible relative drift of 1-3% and a rising basket that cannot be hedged (Coval & Shumway 2001; Bakshi & Kapadia 2003).

Real-contract check: up to 6 of the ~30 expired contracts, spent on ND dev events. Reported only.

families.name: RF: Fear-gated de-risking overlay (the fear model as a risk forecaster; no return claim, not a Holm family)
families.source_lens: Risk management and portfolio construction (designer 2, R1), cut to 3 variants. This family carries the requirement that one family uses the model as a risk forecaster.
families.mechanism:
Volatility clusters, but short-horizon expected returns do not rise in proportion to variance. Cutting exposure when forecast risk is high therefore improves risk-adjusted returns (Fleming, Kirby & Ostdiek 2001 JF; Moreira & Muir 2017 JF; Harvey et al. 2018 JPM). The effect is stronger when exposure changes only in extreme states (Bongaerts, Kang & van Dijk 2020 FAJ), and the market-level version survives costs best (Barroso & Detzel 2021 JFE).

The evidence is fragile out of sample:
- Real-time versions often fail to beat buy-and-hold on mean return (Cederburg, O'Doherty, Wang & Yan 2020 JFE).
- An in-sample scaling constant is a look-ahead (Liu, Tang & Zhou 2019).
The claim here is therefore only a reduction in variance and tail risk at little cost.

The fear model's role:
- M_pct is a validated thermometer (it tracks VXN, Spearman 0.55 out of sample), and the stressed regime persists for weeks. That persistence is what makes a gate useful.
- HAR supplies the level of basket volatility. M adds little to HAR (H4 failed), so the always-on HAR variant serves as the comparator without fear input.

RF never generates a high-conviction trade by itself. It scales the core AI holdings and feeds the risk framework.
families.entry_rule:
Decided at each full-session close t; a half-day keeps E_t = E_t-1.

Inputs:
- M_pct_t: point-in-time in backtests, frozen v3 live.
- sigma_hat_t: a recursive HAR forecast of the equal-weight basket's next-5-session daily volatility. Built with validate.har_design(R), where R = engine.basket_legs(prices)['cc'] (equal-weight close-to-close return of tradable names). OLS on rows s <= t-5, from the first complete row in 2023, with at least 60 rows. sigma_hat_t = exp(fitted value).
- sigma_star_t = median of sigma_hat_s over every s <= t that has a forecast (a causal target).

Exposure E_t in [0.25, 1] on the basket:

RF1 (staircase):
- E starts at 1.
- If M_pct_t >= 1.5: E_t = 0.5.
- Else, if M_pct_t < 1.0 and E_t-1 < 1: E_t = min(1, E_t-1 + 0.25).
- Otherwise: E_t = E_t-1.

RF2 (gated volatility target):
- A stress state switches on at any close with M_pct_t >= 1.5. It switches off at the first full-session close with M_pct_t < 1.0.
- While the state is on: E_t = clip(sigma_star_t / sigma_hat_t, 0.25, 1).
- After it switches off: E_t = min(1, E_t-1 + 0.25) at each full session with M_pct_t < 1.0. E is held while 1.0 <= M_pct_t < 1.5, and the state comes back on at M_pct_t >= 1.5.

RF3 (comparator without fear input):
- target = clip(sigma_star_t / sigma_hat_t, 0.25, 1).
- E_t = target if |target - E_t-1| >= 0.10; otherwise E_t = E_t-1.
families.execution:
Test: engine.run_exposure(E, engine.basket_legs(prices), cost_bps=10, delay=1).
- Weight E_t in the daily-rebalanced equal-weight basket, decided at close t and traded at the open of t+1. The overnight leg is held at the previous weight and the intraday leg at the new one.
- Cost: 10 bps x |change in E|, charged at the open (25 bps stress test).
- The remainder sits in cash at 0%.
- Delay check: delay=2.

Live:
- RF applies to the user's core AI holdings, at strategic weight K of NAV set by the user. If there are none, RF is display-only.
- Target core delta = K x E_t, reached by selling or buying shares pro rata at the open of t+1, or through the covered-call expression.
- RF does not scale SR or ND tickets; the sizing framework handles their risk.
families.exit_rule: Re-risking follows the state machines above: a staircase of +0.25 per full session with M_pct_t < 1.0, and for RF3 a continuous target with a 0.10 band. No price stops and no time limit.
variants: RF1 (primary): staircase on fear alone. E = 0.5 at M_pct >= 1.5; +0.25 per full session with M_pct < 1.0, until E = 1.
RF2: fear-gated volatility target. Inside the state, E = clip(sigma_star/sigma_hat, 0.25, 1); a staircase back to 1 afterwards.
RF3: always-on inverse-volatility target from HAR alone (no fear input), with a 0.10 no-trade band. The comparator that measures what the fear gate adds.
families.predicted_signature:
Predicted:
- (1) The gain is in the variance term. Variance is at least 15% below the static mix's, while the timing-of-mean term is indistinguishable from zero; no return skill is claimed.
- (2) Moreira-Muir: the basket's return per unit of realized variance is lower on sessions with E < 1 than on sessions with E = 1.
- (3) The gain comes from multi-week stressed episodes. Single-spike, V-shaped episodes contribute zero or less.
- (4) The one-day delay keeps at least 2/3 of the variance gain.
- (5) Fear gating helps: the mean d of RF2 >= that of RF3.

ADOPTION, pre-declared. It replaces SPA and Holm because nothing is claimed about returns.
- Choose the variant by the 1-SE rule on mean d_t, in declared order (RF1, RF2, RF3).
- Adopt it only if all of the following hold on dev (2024-01-02..2025-12-31):
  - (A1) variance ratio <= 0.85;
  - (A2) non-inferiority: mean d_t >= -0.5 s.e. at 10 bps, at 25 bps, and with a one-day delay;
  - (A3) CVaR95 and maximum drawdown are both no worse than the static mix's.
- CONFIRMED additionally requires A1 and A2 on the 2026 holdout. Only a confirmed RF is applied live; otherwise it is display-only.

Signatures (2)-(5) are reported.
families.power_note:
Counts use signal-side data only (point-in-time M_pct run through the RF1 state machine).
- Dev: 12 de-risk episodes; 141 of 502 sessions at reduced exposure; 38 exposure changes; mean E 0.89 in 2024 and 0.84 in 2025.
- 2026: 5 episodes; 50 of 228 sessions at reduced exposure.

Point-in-time M_pct reads >= 1.5 on 18% of dev sessions but only 9% of 2026 sessions, because the early refits were trained on calmer data. The gate is effectively stricter in 2026 and live.

With basket volatility of about 1.8%/day in calm and 3.5% in stress, the expected certainty-equivalent gain at gamma = 5 is about 3-5% a year, against noise of about 6-10% a year. That gives t of about 0.4-0.8, so a return-type gate cannot pass and would waste a Holm slot.

Variance and tails are estimated far more precisely than means, which is why adoption rests on A1-A3. The non-inferiority margin (-0.5 s.e.) is lenient by design: adoption means 'reduces risk at little measured cost', never 'adds return'.
families.options_expression:
Live, and on core holdings only.

When E_t < 1, for core shares in the nine most liquid names (MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, AVGO, AMD, TSM, ORCL):
- Candidate: the 30-45 DTE call nearest +0.35 delta (accept 0.30-0.40), with spread <= 10%, OI >= 250 and no earnings before expiry.
- If rho = IV_call x sqrt(D/365) / sigma_tilde_i(h) >= 1.25, write covered calls instead of selling shares. Contracts = floor((1 - E_t) x shares / (100 x delta)), capped at floor(shares / 100). This keeps the upside to the strike in a V-shaped rebound, the overlay's main failure mode, and harvests the stress-inflated IV (Whaley 2002; Israelov & Nielsen 2015).
- Otherwise, sell (1 - E_t) of the position at the open.

When E_t rises:
- Let the calls expire, or buy them back at the open.
- To re-enter after selling shares: sell 21-35 DTE cash-secured puts at delta -0.25 to -0.30 if rho >= 1.25; otherwise buy shares at the open.

No protective puts: in stress they are bought at peak IV, and in calm their spread costs across names exceed the benefit.

There is no IV history to test this, so options use is tracked on paper first.

rejected.name: Good news in bad times: distraction drift (designer 1, family B)
rejected.reason:
Rejected for five reasons:
- It is the family most exposed to the hindsight bias. Names whose good news led to sustained rallies are how the 2026 AI-winner list was formed, and the 2026 holdout shares that selection, so a pass would not be credible.
- Drift after news in large caps has largely disappeared (Chordia et al. 2009; Martineau 2022).
- Power is low: about 160 dev events with a 20-session residual s.d. of 11-13%, only 2 events in 2025Q2, and clustering in earnings seasons.
- Its news-drift mechanism is already tested on the bearish side (ND), where the bias runs against it.
- As a third Holm family it would lower the best family's threshold from 0.05 to 0.033.

rejected.name: Idiosyncratic intraday flush reversal sold as puts (designer 3, family C)
rejected.reason:
Not declared as a family. Its rule survives as two contrasts: SR's shock-type contrast and ND's no-news contrast. Reasons:
- Nagel (2012) predicts a small liquidity premium in calm markets.
- The price-only no-news proxy is weak: intraday news is common (downgrades, conference remarks, short reports, policy headlines).
- About 96-103 dev events need roughly 2% per 5 sessions, at the top of published no-news reversal magnitudes.
- The hindsight bias runs in its favor.
- As a third Holm family it would cut SR's threshold to 0.033.

rejected.name: Risk-timed, staggered re-entry after systemic hits (designer 2, R3)
rejected.reason:
Merged into SR, which has the same mechanism, events and benchmark. What was not carried over, and why:
- Its raw-hit selection (x >= 3 and Z >= 2) is dominated by beta, which is what made the earlier Z >= 2.5 study flip sign.
- Its timing variants (wait for P_panic < 0.20 within 5 sessions; buy thirds at t+1..t+3) were not declared. The reversal is predicted to come early, and the one-day-delay gate already measures timing sensitivity.
- Equal-risk sizing (1/sigma) moved to live sizing, because the declared test portfolio is equal weight.

rejected.name: Shock-typed exits as a separate family (designer 2, R2), including its V3 and V4
rejected.reason:
Merged into ND. The events are the same idiosyncratic information shocks, and 'sell and redistribute over the basket' equals ND's short-information cohort test up to 1/N scaling. Changes:
- V3 (untyped stop) dropped as a variant. A foil predicted to lose only adds SPA dimensions and could be picked by the 1-SE rule; the typed contrast is reported instead.
- V4 (re-admit at Z < 1) dropped. A state-dependent exit does not fit fixed-H cohorts, and Z is smoothed by the HMM.
- The broad x >= 3 & Z >= 2 trigger is replaced by ND's news proxy based on the overnight gap, so that the information-split signature can be tested.

rejected.name: Fear-gated overlay as a Holm alpha family (designer 2, R1 under SPA), and its RF4 inverse-variance variant
rejected.reason: The expected t on any return-type statistic is 0.4-0.8, so a Holm slot would be wasted. It is kept as RF, with a pre-declared non-alpha adoption path (variance, tails, non-inferiority). RF4 (the Moreira-Muir form) was dropped to save variants, since RF3 already tests always-on targeting.

rejected.name: Undeclared variant settings
rejected.reason:
- Designer 3's A3 (M_pct >= 2.0): only 32 dev days in 7 episodes.
- Designer 3's A1 threshold of 1.5: unstable across refits. Point-in-time M_pct >= 1.5 holds on 18% of dev sessions but 9% of 2026 sessions, while >= 1.0 holds steadily on about 30%, so SR3 uses 1.0.
- Designer 3's v <= -1 with cap 5: folded into SR's v <= -1.5 with cap 10.
- ND dose variants (x >= 4, v <= -3, g_seg <= -3): 74-80% overlap with ND1, so near-duplicates.
- Relative-volume confirmation for ND: the high-volume return premium (Gervais, Kaniel & Mingelgrin 2001) works against a bearish drift.
- ND with H = 60: overlaps H = 40 and loses dev signals after October 2025.

rejected.name: Options-only variance-premium trade after systemic spikes (options lens)
rejected.reason: There is no historical IV surface, there are only 7-10 market episodes, and its delta leg has already failed (buying the basket at M >= 2). The premium idea lives on in SR's cash-secured-put expression.

rejected.name: Long puts as a traded bearish family; option thresholds tuned on a dev payoff replay
rejected.reason:
Long puts stay on paper unless ND reaches tier 2. Theta, the variance premium and 3-10% spreads exceed a plausible 1-3% relative drift (Coval & Shumway 2001; Bakshi & Kapadia 2003).

Designer 3's lambda_S and lambda_C, derived from a dev payoff replay, are replaced by fixed thresholds declared now: sell premium at rho >= 1.25, buy at rho <= 0.90. No parameter is left to be tuned, and the replay is reported only.

rejected.name: IVOL, MAX/lottery, betting-against-beta, momentum crashes, and volatility-managed basket timing as alpha (designer 1's declined list)
rejected.reason: Agreed with the designer. Their payoffs sit in the short leg (Stambaugh, Yu & Yuan 2015), the hindsight universe biases them, and market-level timing has only 4-8 episodes in two years (Cederburg et al. 2020).

rejected.name: Protective puts; covered calls on SR or ND positions; price stops
rejected.reason:
- Protective puts are bought at peak IV.
- Covered calls sell the rebound SR predicts; only the CSP's buy-write twin is allowed.
- Price stops destroy value on positions that mean-revert and add value only under positive autocorrelation (Kaminski & Lo 2014; Lo & Remorov 2017). Exits are by time, or typed exits.

sizing_and_risk:
0. SCOPE
- Selection uses only the unconstrained test portfolios declared for each family.
- Everything below is the live implementation. It is also simulated on dev and on 2026 as a reported check, but never used as a selection input.
- Account: cash, no margin, long-only shares, level-2 options. NAV = account equity.

1. RISK YARDSTICK (the fear model as a risk forecaster)
For name i at close t and horizon h sessions:
- U_i = sum over j = 1..h of (p_i,t A^j) . s^2 (risk.forward_var_units).
  - p = (P_calm, P_stressed, P_panic).
  - A and s come from the refit in force; frozen v3 live.
- Log regime multiplier: l_i = 0.5 ln(U_i / h).
- Shrink halfway toward the day's cross-sectional mean, because the within-day calibration slope on dev is 0.50: l~_i = 0.5 l_i + 0.5 mean_j(l_j), over eligible names.
- sigma_tilde_i(h) = kappa_h x sigma_i,t x sqrt(h) x exp(l~_i).
- kappa_h = sqrt(sum RV / sum (sigma_tilde / kappa_h)^2) over dev eligible stock-days, where RV_i,t(h) = sum over j = 1..h of r_i,t+j^2.
  - Computed once on dev for h in {1, 5, 10, 20, 40}.
  - Any other h uses the nearest of these.

Validation, run once on dev:
- Compare the QLIKE loss (Patton 2011) of sigma_tilde^2 against RV with that of EWMA(0.94), level-calibrated the same way, at h = 5 and h = 20.
- If the fear yardstick's mean QLIKE is worse than EWMA's by more than 1 s.e. at either h, use EWMA everywhere, for sizing and for the options rho. The s.e. comes from a stationary bootstrap over days (block 20).
- Report Kupiec and Christoffersen coverage of 1-day 95% and 99% VaR for the basket and for random 10-name books.

Equicorrelation:
- rho_t = max of the 21-session and 63-session averages of the off-diagonal entries of the sample correlation matrix.
- The matrix is built from eligible names' daily log returns (pairwise complete).

2. EDGE PER ADOPTED FAMILY f (shrinkage first, then fractional Kelly)
- e_j = per-event net excess at 10 bps for the adopted variant, on dev events plus 2026 events. The 2026 events enter only after the single holdout read.
- IRhat_f = mean(e) / sd(e), the per-trade information ratio.
- N_eff = number of distinct ISO weeks with at least one entry.
- Prior: IR ~ N(0, 0.05^2). It is tight on purpose: H5 failed, the panic-buy edge flipped sign, there are only two years of data, and several families are being tested.
- IR_post = IRhat x 0.0025 / (0.0025 + 1/N_eff).
- If IR_post <= 0, the family is tier 0.
- The equity premium never counts as edge.
- Re-estimate IR_post every quarter as N_eff grows.

3. PER-TICKET RISK BUDGET RB
RB is a fraction of NAV equal to the 1-s.d. loss over the holding period.
- RB = min(TierCap, 0.25 x IR_post).
- Why a quarter of Kelly: under full Kelly a bet's 1-s.d. P/L equals its IR. With a fraction c of Kelly, the chance of ever losing half the capital is 0.5^(2/c - 1): 50% at full Kelly, 12.5% at half, 0.8% at a quarter (Thorp 2006; MacLean, Thorp & Ziemba 2011).
- Correlated bets: let n = the number of this family's positions opened in the last 5 sessions, including today's. Then RB <- RB / (1 + (n - 1) x rho).
  - rho = rho_t for SR.
  - rho = 0.3 for ND.

4. SIZE
- Shares: notional = RB x NAV / sigma_tilde_i(H). Use total, not residual, volatility, because beta cannot be hedged.
- CSP: contracts = floor(notional / (100 x strike)). Its notional never exceeds the share version's.
- Long call: dollar delta about equal to the notional; premium <= min(30% of notional, 1% of NAV).
- ND long put: premium <= min(RB x NAV, 0.5% of NAV).

5. HARD CAPS
Apply the caps in the order listed. A breach is fixed by scaling down the day's NEW tickets pro rata. Existing positions are never force-sold, except by their own exits.
- Per name: <= 10% of NAV (shares + CSP strike notional + call dollar delta). <= 5% if q_next_i,t >= 0.10 or P_panic_i,t >= 0.5 at the signal.
- Per segment: <= 30% of NAV. Compute, foundry_memory and semicap combined: <= 45%.
- Per family and in total:
  - SR gross <= 40% of NAV;
  - ND open put premium <= 2% of NAV;
  - total long-option premium <= 4% of NAV;
  - all tactical gross <= 60% of NAV.
- Cash: shares + CSP strike notional + premium <= 100% of NAV.
- Liquidity: each order <= 1% of the name's 20-session median dollar volume.
- Ex-ante volatility, computed with sigma_tilde_i(1), equicorrelation rho_t and delta-equivalent options:
  - whole book <= 30% annualized;
  - tactical sleeve <= 12%;
  - any single family <= 6%.
- One-day stress loss <= 10% of NAV. In the scenario, every share and CSP position falls 3 x sigma_tilde_i(1) at once (rho = 1). Long options lose at most their premium.
- Tail monitor: sum over i of w_i x q_next_i x 3 x sigma_i <= 2% of NAV.

6. STOPS AND EXITS
- No price stops anywhere.
- Exits are only:
  - time exits;
  - ND typed exits on core holdings, if ND is adopted;
  - the RF exposure target.
- Use long options when a hard loss cap is wanted.

7. BRAKES AND GOVERNANCE
- Tactical drawdown >= 8% of NAV: halve every new RB.
- Tactical drawdown >= 12%: open no new tactical tickets (open ones run to their exits) and start a review.
- Normal budgets return when the drawdown is back below 4%, or after 60 sessions with a logged review.
- Account circuit breaker: no new cohorts while equity is more than 15% below its peak. Resume once it is back within 10%.
- Sequential guard, pre-registered for the paper and live test: after every 25 closed events, suspend a family whose running mean net excess is below its dev estimate minus 2 s.e.

8. EXECUTION
- Signals at the close; orders at the next open.
- Shares: market-on-open orders, matching the test.
- Options:
  - limit at mid, conceding at most 1/4 of the spread, between 09:45 and 10:30 ET;
  - skip if the spread is more than 10% of mid or open interest is below 250;
  - no option orders on half-days;
  - never hold a short-dated option through an earnings date.

9. EXPIRED-CONTRACT BUDGET
- Up to 12 contracts for SR's CSP enablement check.
- Up to 6 for ND.
- The rest is reserved for live spot checks.

WORKED EXAMPLE (SR at tier 2)
- IRhat = 0.15 and N_eff = 100 give IR_post = 0.03, so RB = min(0.5%, 0.75%) = 0.5% of NAV.
- Eight SR positions were opened in the last 5 sessions and rho_t = 0.55, so RB = 0.5% / (1 + 7 x 0.55) = 0.103% of NAV.
- With sigma_tilde_i(5) = 6.5%, the notional is 1.6% of NAV per name, about 13% of NAV for the 8 names.
